subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Continues the school Drive Quran folder progression (TPS Quran Tracker tajweed rules) into Year 11; classical tajweed (Hafs 'an 'Asim) and tadabbur method; Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Tajweed mastery and Al-Kahf consolidation
lessons.title: The tajweed map: Al-Fatihah line by line
lessons.bigQuestion: You recite Al-Fatihah at least 17 times a day. If you audited it today, would it pass every rule?
objectives: To understand how the six families of tajweed rules fit together, using Al-Fatihah as the map
successCriteria: All: name the six families of rules
Most: identify a rule from each family in Al-Fatihah
Some: recite Al-Fatihah with every rule named and applied
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: perfecting the surah we recite in every rak'ah

keywords.def: giving each letter its right and its rules

hook.text: You recite Al-Fatihah at least 17 times a day. If you audited it today, would it pass every rule?
hook.a: Many find small slips (madd, heavy letters, ض). The most recited surah deserves the most care.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have certainly given you seven of the often repeated and the great Qur'an' (Al-Hijr 15:87). The Prophet ﷺ called Al-Fatihah the seven often-repeated (al-sab' al-mathani) (Bukhari).

teach.heading: Six families of rules
teach.note: Bismillah. Year 11 is mastery: rules automatic, then passing the Qur'an on.

items: Raa and laam: heavy or light
Waqf and ibtida': stopping and starting

teach.heading: Al-Fatihah: the map
teach.note: Name the family for each.

teach.heading: Juz' Tabarak with the map
bullets: Name one rule from each family
teach.note: This week's revision: Juz' 29 (67 to 77).

misconception.wrong: ٱلضَّآلِّينَ with 2 counts and ض like د
misconception.right: 6 counts (madd lazim); ض from the side of the tongue

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: The madd in «وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ» before the shaddah is ...
check.why: Alif followed by a letter with shaddah (a permanent sukoon) in the word: madd lazim kalimi, 6.

practice.q: Map Al-Fatihah 1:4 «مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ» to the six families.
practice.a: مَٰلِكِ: small alif madd 2; يَوْمِ: و sakin after fathah (leen when stopping only); ٱلدِّينِ: sun letter د, madd 'arid at the stop.
practice.model: I do: مَٰلِكِ: small alif, natural madd 2. يَوْمِ: the waw is leen; we are not stopping, so no lengthening. ٱلدِّينِ: د is a sun letter; stopping: 'arid 2, 4 or 6.

practice.q: «لِلَّهِ»: the laam is ...

independent.q: Map Al-Mulk 67:1 to 2 to the six families (pupil PDF). Today's rota group recites Juz' Tabarak placement surahs to the teacher.
independent.a: e.g. شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌ ikhfa; ٱلْمُلْكُ moon letter; عَمَلًۭا ۚ وَهُوَ idgham if joined; ٱلْعَزِيزُ moon letter; ۚ ja'iz stop; قَدِيرٌ 'arid at a stop.
independent.model: The teacher maps تَبَٰرَكَ: small alif madd 2; ٱلَّذِى: sun letter laam.

independent.q: Extend: name the family you find hardest and one practice for it.
independent.a: Personal target with a practice plan.

independent.q: Stretch: explain the difference between madd lazim and madd 'arid.
independent.a: Lazim: permanent sukoon in the word, always 6; 'arid: sukoon only from stopping, 2, 4 or 6.

exit.q: How many families on the map?
Back to our ponder: You recite Al-Fatihah at least 17 times a day. If you audited it today, would it pass every rule?
exit.a: Many find small slips (madd, heavy letters, ض). The most recited surah deserves the most care.

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Fatihah slowly with the map once a day and revise Juz' Tabarak (two surahs a day); log it.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.

Pupil PDF worksheet: The tajweed map rule card and examples
Teacher's own recitation, spoken only (no melody exercises or audio with music)
Portal revision log (pupil ticks daily revision; parent initials)

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Tajweed mastery and Al-Kahf consolidation
lessons.title: Mistakes in recitation: spotting and correcting kindly
lessons.bigQuestion: If someone corrects your recitation in front of others, how do you want them to do it?
objectives: To understand the difference between clear and hidden mistakes (lahn jali and lahn khafi) and correct them with good manners
successCriteria: All: give one example of lahn jali and one of lahn khafi
Most: correct a partner's mistake precisely and kindly
Some: explain why lahn jali must be fixed first
lessons.smsc: Social: correcting others with kindness and accepting correction humbly

keywords.def: a mistake in recitation: jali (clear) or khafi (hidden)
a clear mistake: letter or vowel changed
a hidden mistake: a rule not fully applied

hook.text: If someone corrects your recitation in front of others, how do you want them to do it?
hook.a: Gently, precisely and privately where possible; this is how we correct others too.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The one who is skilled in the Qur'an will be with the noble and righteous scribes, and the one who recites it with difficulty, stumbling, has two rewards' (Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: Recite Al-Mulk 67:3 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?
How many families on the tajweed map?

teach.heading: Two kinds of mistake
teach.note: Bismillah.

teach.heading: Clear mistakes in Al-Fatihah
bullets: ص said as س in ٱلصِّرَٰطَ
teach.note: Each changes a letter or vowel. Say why each matters.

teach.heading: Correcting with adab
bullets: Wait for the end of the ayah
Name the ayah, word and fix
Thank the person who corrects you
teach.note: Model a respectful correction.

misconception.wrong: Interrupting mid-word and listing every slip
misconception.right: Wait, then give one precise correction, starting with any lahn jali

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

options: Lahn jali: it changes the meaning
check.why: A changed vowel that changes 'You favoured' into 'I favoured' is a clear mistake.

practice.q: Classify: (a) short muttasil in 36:6 ءَابَآؤُهُمْ; (b) ح said as ه in ٱلْحَكِيمِ (36:2).
practice.a: (a) lahn khafi (rule not fully applied); (b) lahn jali (letter changed).
practice.model: I do: (a) the words are right but the madd is short: hidden mistake. (b) ح became ه: a different letter: clear mistake, fix first.

practice.q: Which to fix first?

independent.q: Breakout pairs: recite Ya-Sin 36:1 to 12 (or read it from the mushaf if not yet memorised); your partner records any lahn jali and khafi on the pupil PDF. Today's rota group recites to the teacher.
independent.a: Partner sheet with mistakes classified and one correction given kindly.
independent.model: The teacher and a volunteer model one round with a kind correction.

independent.q: Extend: write your own three most common lahn and how you will fix them.
independent.a: Personal list.

independent.q: Stretch: explain why a mistake of the tongue is forgiven but practice is still required.
independent.a: Two rewards for the one who struggles (Bukhari and Muslim), yet we strive to recite as revealed.

exit.q: Weak ghunnah is ...
Back to our ponder: If someone corrects your recitation in front of others, how do you want them to do it?
exit.a: Gently, precisely and privately where possible; this is how we correct others too.

lessons.homework: Recite Ya-Sin 36:1 to 12 to a parent; note one lahn khafi to fix; log it.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Tajweed mastery and Al-Kahf consolidation
lessons.title: Surat Al-Kahf 18:1-5: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ told us that memorising the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal. Why might these ayat protect?
objectives: To memorise Al-Kahf 18:1-5 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 18:1-5 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 18:1-5 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 18:1-5 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: protection through firm belief and the Qur'an

hook.text: The Prophet ﷺ told us that memorising the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal. Why might these ayat protect?
hook.a: They affirm the straight Book, the reward of believers and the warning against false claims about Allah: firm belief protects (18:1 to 5).

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever memorises ten ayat from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal' (Muslim). Allah says: 'All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance' (Al-Kahf 18:1).

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Kahf 18:1-5
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 18:1-5 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُۥ عِوَجَا ۜ (١) قَيِّمًۭا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًۭا شَدِيدًۭا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًۭا (٢) مَّٰكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًۭا (٣) وَيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًۭا (٤) مَّا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍۢ وَلَا لِءَابَآئِهِمْ ۚ كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةًۭ تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ ۚ إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًۭا (٥)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: [All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance.
[He has made it] straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward
In which they will remain forever
And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."
They have no knowledge of it, nor had their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 18:1-5 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

options: A brief silent pause, no new breath
check.why: Saktah: a short pause without taking breath; it separates 'no deviance' from 'straight'.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Kahf 18:1-5 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 18:1-5 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 18:1-5. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 18:1-5 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: In the portal box, explain what 18:4 to 5 warn against.
independent.a: Saying that Allah has taken a son: a grave word without knowledge.

independent.q: Explain why the saktah protects the meaning of 18:1 to 2.
independent.a: Without it, قَيِّمًا could seem to describe 'deviance'; the pause makes clear 'straight' describes the Book.

exit.q: Al-Kahf 18:3: «مَّٰكِثِينَ ...» Which word comes next?
Back to our ponder: The Prophet ﷺ told us that memorising the first ten ayat of Al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal. Why might these ayat protect?
exit.a: They affirm the straight Book, the reward of believers and the warning against false claims about Allah: firm belief protects (18:1 to 5).

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Kahf 18:1-5 to a parent three times a day and revise Juz' Tabarak (one surah) and Juz' 'Amma block of the day; tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: shorter chunks (one ayah), the pupil PDF with each word spaced, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: link to the next ayat and explain one rule to the class.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Kahf 18:6-10: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Young men left everything and took shelter in a cave, praying for mercy and guidance. What would make someone do that?
objectives: To memorise Al-Kahf 18:6-10 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 18:6-10 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 18:6-10 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 18:6-10 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: young people holding firm to faith and turning to Allah in du'a

keywords.def: the inscription (or the name linked with the people of the cave)

hook.text: Young men left everything and took shelter in a cave, praying for mercy and guidance. What would make someone do that?
hook.a: Protecting their faith; they asked Allah for mercy and right guidance (18:10).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: '[Mention] when the youths retreated to the cave and said: Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance' (Al-Kahf 18:10).

starter.q: Recite Al-Kahf 18:3 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Kahf 18:6-10
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 18:6-10 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: فَلَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعٌۭ نَّفْسَكَ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا (٦) إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ زِينَةًۭ لَّهَا لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًۭا (٧) وَإِنَّا لَجَٰعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيْهَا صَعِيدًۭا جُرُزًا (٨) أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْكَهْفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا۟ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا (٩) إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةًۭ وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًۭا (١٠)

bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Then perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, [O Muhammad], if they do not believe in this message, [and] out of sorrow.
Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.
And indeed, We will make that which is upon it [into] a barren ground.
Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder?
[Mention] when the youths retreated to the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance."

teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 18:6-10 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.

Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: What did the youths ask for in 18:10?
check.why: 18:10: 'grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance'.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Kahf 18:6-10 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 18:6-10 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 18:6-10. Ayah 6: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 7 the same way. Then link: recite 6 and 7 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 18:6-10 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: In the portal box, write the du'a of 18:10 in Arabic and its meaning, and when you might use it.
independent.a: رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةًۭ وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًۭا: before a decision or exam.

independent.q: Recite 18:1 to 10 with the saktah.
independent.a: All ten ayat, no prompts.

Back to our ponder: Young men left everything and took shelter in a cave, praying for mercy and guidance. What would make someone do that?

lessons.title: Al-Fatihah: a conversation with Allah
objectives: Explain the meaning of each ayah of Al-Fatihah
Describe the hadith of the prayer divided in two
Reflect on how to pray with presence

keywords.def: praise coupled with love and glorification
humility and presence of heart in prayer

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Say the meaning of ar-Rahman ar-Rahim.

teach.heading: Ayat 1-4: Who Allah is
bullets: Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds
The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
Master of the Day of Recompense
teach.note: Take each phrase slowly in English. In the Hafs recitation we read مَالِكِ, Master. Ask: what do the names Rabb, Rahman, Rahim and Malik teach us? Care, mercy and accountability together.

teach.heading: Ayat 5-7: What we ask
bullets: You alone we worship and seek help from
Guide us to the straight path
The path of those You blessed, not those who went astray
teach.note: Ayah 5 is the turning point from speaking about Allah to speaking to Him. Ayah 6 is the greatest need: guidance. Ayah 7 describes the path through the blessed ones. Scholars explain the two groups to avoid as those who know the truth and turn away, and those who lose the way.

teach.heading: The prayer divided
bullets: Sahih Muslim: Allah says He divided the prayer
The servant says Alhamdu lillah; Allah says: My servant praised Me
Half is for Allah, half for the servant
teach.note: The hadith is reported by Abu Hurayrah in Sahih Muslim. When the servant says each part, Allah responds. When the servant says 'You alone we worship and seek help from', Allah says that is between Him and His servant, and the servant will have what he asks. Ask: how does this change how you say the Fatihah in salah?

teach.heading: Praying with presence
bullets: Say each ayah as a reply
Think of the meaning, not only the sound
teach.note: Teach practical techniques: slow down slightly, think of the response from Allah, and focus on one phrase each prayer. Pupils practise silently. Note that khushu' is a goal built over time; do not discourage those who struggle.

teach.heading: My tadabbur
bullets: Write what it asks of you
teach.note: Pupils write a short piece connecting one ayah to a personal change, such as being more grateful (ayah 2) or more mindful of accountability (ayah 4). Share one anonymously.

practice: What happens, according to the hadith, when the servant says 'Alhamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin'?
Which ayah is the turning point from speaking about Allah to speaking to Him?
What are we asking for in ayah 6?
independent: Write a one-line meaning for each ayah
Draw the dialogue between servant and Lord
Write a short tadabbur on one ayah
exit: Which ayah of Al-Fatihah speaks most to you now?
What is one way to bring more presence to your recitation in salah?

lessons.title: Reading translations and tafsir wisely
objectives: Explain what a translation of the Qur'an can and cannot do
Use context to avoid misreading an ayah
Know when to ask a qualified scholar

keywords.def: an attempt to express the meaning in another language
the surrounding words, ayat and circumstances
the reasons or occasions of revelation

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
What are the sources of tafsir?
What is the difference between tafsir and tadabbur?

teach.heading: What translation can do
bullets: It renders meanings, not the Qur'an itself
The Arabic text is the Qur'an
teach.note: Explain that a translation is a human attempt at the meaning and cannot replace the Arabic. Compare two English renderings of 1:5 if available. Ask: why might two translators choose different words?

teach.heading: Always read the whole sentence
bullets: Quote 4:43: do not approach prayer while intoxicated
The ayah continues: until you know what you say
teach.note: 4:43 is a useful example: the ayah continues with 'until you know what you are saying'. Show how stopping early would give a false impression. Similarly 107:4-5: 'woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer'. Ask: what changes when we read the whole phrase?

teach.heading: Context and sources
bullets: Know the Arabic language and the Sunnah
teach.note: 2:256 says there is no compulsion in religion, and the following words say that the right path has become distinct from error. Show how a tafsir explains the context. Name tafsirs such as Tafsir al-Tabari, Tafsir Ibn Kathir and Tafsir al-Sa'di. Pupils choose one to look up.

teach.heading: Pitfalls to avoid
bullets: Applying ayat to modern events without knowledge
teach.note: Warn against claiming that a personal idea is the meaning of an ayah. Explain that qualified scholars study Arabic, Qur'an sciences and the Sunnah. A good habit: say 'scholars have said...' and cite. Ask: what is the harm of quoting an ayah without context?

teach.heading: When to ask
bullets: Say 'I do not know' when needed
teach.note: Teach humility: knowing the limits of our knowledge is part of good adab. Pupils write a question they would take to a scholar. Close with a dua for understanding.

practice: Complete 4:43: 'do not approach prayer while intoxicated, until...'
Why is it important to read the full ayah?
independent: Find the full context of 2:256 in a tafsir and summarise it
Rewrite a mis-quoted half ayah with its full text
Write a code of conduct for quoting the Qur'an
exit: Why can a translation never replace the Arabic?
Name one way to avoid misusing an ayah.
lessons.homework: Choose an ayah you know, read its tafsir and write a short summary with its context.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scaffolded tafsir reading with a glossary. Stretch: compare two tafsir explanations of one ayah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Teaching, recital and a lifelong plan
lessons.title: Teaching the Qur'an: planning a mini lesson
objectives: Explain why teaching the Qur'an is valued
Plan a five-minute mini lesson on one tajweed rule
Give and receive feedback on teaching

keywords.def: to show clearly how something is done
repeat after the teacher, one phrase at a time

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
What is one rule you can explain confidently?

teach.heading: A great reward
bullets: Bukhari: the best of you learn the Qur'an and teach it
teach.note: Quote the hadith reported by Uthman in Sahih al-Bukhari: the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it. Ask: why is teaching a form of ihsan? Remind pupils to teach for Allah, not to impress.

teach.heading: Plan a mini lesson
bullets: Choose one rule and one example
Let the learner echo, then try alone
teach.note: Show the structure: aim, model, echo, practise, check. Model with a rule such as ikhfa using a short phrase. Pupils choose their own rule and an ayah as the example. Ask: which examples are clearest?

teach.heading: Teaching well
bullets: Correct one thing at a time
teach.note: Link to the lesson on correction. Give feedback phrases. Remind pupils that a teacher also learns: when you teach, you notice your own mistakes. Ask: what would you say to someone who is nervous?

teach.heading: Know your limits
teach.note: Teach humility: pupils may teach basic rules to family and younger pupils but should refer to qualified teachers for difficult questions. Discuss: who taught you the Qur'an? Make dua for them.

teach.heading: Peer practice
bullets: Teach your mini lesson to a partner
Partner gives one strength, one target
teach.note: In breakout pairs, pupils deliver the five-minute lesson. The partner uses the checklist. Return to the main room and share one good idea. Collect plans for display.

practice: What does the hadith in Bukhari say about the best of us?

lessons.homework: Teach your mini lesson to a family member or younger sibling and note what went well.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: mini lesson template with sentence frames. Stretch: plan a series of three short lessons on one theme.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Teaching, recital and a lifelong plan
lessons.title: Recital assessment and a lifelong plan with the Qur'an
objectives: Recite a chosen passage with the rubric
Self-assess and peer-assess
Write a plan for keeping and living by the Qur'an

keywords.def: a set of criteria for judging quality

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Which passage will you recite today?

teach.heading: Prepare
teach.note: Give five minutes to prepare quietly. Remind pupils of adab: sincere intention, calm place, a short dua. Reduce nerves; this is a chance to show growth over the years.

teach.heading: Rubric
teach.note: Share the rubric. Pupils recite individually or in pairs. Mark with the rubric. Give feedback as one strength, one target, one action. Make it warm and encouraging.

teach.heading: Recite and listen
teach.note: Pupils recite in turn. The listener practises adab: silence, attention and kindness. Remind them of 7:204 on listening to the Qur'an. Keep good humour and respect.

teach.heading: Look back
teach.note: Pupils return to their tajweed map from Lesson 1. They tick progress and note remaining gaps. Share a few successes aloud and thank Allah for them.

teach.heading: My lifelong plan
bullets: Daily: a few minutes of recitation
teach.note: Pupils write a realistic plan for the years after school: daily time, a revision cycle (sabaq, sabqi, manzil), a teacher or study circle, and one meaning-based habit. Close with a dua for steadfastness and for Allah to make the Qur'an the spring of our hearts.

practice: Which rule family is strongest for you?
Which family needs more work in the future?
independent: Recite your chosen passage for assessment
Complete peer feedback with the rubric
Write your lifelong plan with dates for review
exit: Name one strength in your recitation.
Name one habit you will keep after school.
lessons.homework: Share your plan with a parent or teacher and ask them to check in with you each month.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it' (Bukhari). Year 11 ends with reciting, and with being ready to teach others.

starter.q: Recite Al-Kahf 18:4 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?
The saktah in Al-Kahf is in ...
Ramadan: the Qur'an was revealed in it (2:185)?

teach.heading: How we are assessed
teach.note: Bismillah.

teach.heading: The assessment
bullets: Al-Kahf 18:1 to 10 from a named start
teach.note: One by one; pupils assessed this week in the rota keep that score. Others revise in breakout pairs.

teach.heading: Plan to the final assessment
teach.note: Pupils write the plan on the pupil PDF.

misconception.wrong: Taking a breath at the saktah in 18:1
misconception.right: Pause briefly without breath: عِوَجَا ۜ قَيِّمًا

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Saktah: a short silent pause with no new breath.

practice.q: Self-check: recite 18:1 to 5 and score each rubric row.
practice.model: I do: hifdh 4; makharij 4; rules 3 (ikhfa in بَأْسًۭا شَدِيدًۭا too clear); fluency 4. Target: hum the ikhfa.

practice.q: Al-Kahf 18:1 to 10 protects from ...

independent.q: Mock recitation: recite the named portions to the teacher one by one. While waiting, write your plan to the final assessment on the pupil PDF.
independent.a: Rubric scores and targets recorded in the portal.
independent.model: The teacher runs the first assessment as a model.

independent.q: Extend: write your Ramadan Qur'an plan.
independent.a: Daily plan, logged.

independent.q: Stretch: plan a five-minute mini lesson to teach a younger pupil one rule.
independent.a: Plan with rule, example and a check question.

exit.q: Year 11 Qur'an ends with ...
Back to our ponder: After this mock recitation, what one change would make the biggest difference before the summer?
exit.a: Usually daily revision of the weakest portion and fixing one rule family.

lessons.homework: Follow your plan through Ramadan; log it daily.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.
resources: Slides
Madinah mushaf (Hafs 'an 'Asim), print or the school's approved mushaf app
Pupil PDF worksheet: Mock week recitation against the rubric rule card and examples
Teacher's own recitation, spoken only (no melody exercises or audio with music)
Portal revision log (pupil ticks daily revision; parent initials)
